newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Bullish trade in Worldcom.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Bullish trade in Worldcom.

text.p: Analysts are quick to call the U.S. stock market a market of stocks rather than a stock market, but on Friday, individual equity options were taking a back seat to the broad market's rally, traders said.
But a large trade in WorldCom Inc options at the Pacific Exchange was a highlight, the traders said.
The WorldCom June 30 call traded 17,800 contracts and the June 25 call traded about 10,325 by afternoon.
A market maker in the options said an investor was putting on a position, selling the June 25 calls and buying the June 30s in a three-by-two ratio.
WorldCom shares were up 5/16 at 29-7/8 after reaching a new high for the year at 30-1/16.
"It's pretty optimistic," the market maker said of the options play, which has just a week to be profitable as June options expire at the end of next week.
He added that other than the big WorldCom trades, activity was relatively quiet.
"In general there are buyers of options," he said. "Most of the sellers are sellers who were long at lower levels."
In other activity, a few American Express Co options were active on renewed takeover rumors, traders said.
Both American Express and Citicorp declined comment on rumors the two had resumed merger talks.
Last April, Citicorp chairman and chief executive John Reed confirmed the two companies had talked but said they had failed to reach an agreement.
Shares of American Express were up 3-5/8 at 76-3/4 and Citicorp gained one to 120.
At the American Stock Exchange, where most American Express options trade, the July 75 call traded 2,055, the June 75 put traded 1,465 and the June 70 call traded 1,445. The July 70 put traded 1,050.
"There's a fair amount of speculative buying in the July and near term deep in-the-money contracts," said Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist partners.
But he added that some of the volume was investors closing out positions taken earlier in the year after a research recommendation.
"Volatility, because of that, has remained fairly stable," Schwarz said.
"Rumors have been around and they continue to float around," he said. "Whether they're true or not, nobody seems to know."
He added that, whether the rumor was true or not, the options activity in American Express would not suggest it was widespread.
"There just isn't enough volume and chasing the out-of-the money calls that it's (merger rumor) being reflected in the options," he said.
